title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri International over a packaged drinking water sample it declared unsafe (bromate on first test; PAHs at the referral lab); Bisleri says its water is safe, gives its timeline (Goa plant, six samples 30 Sep 2025, five passed, 12 vs 10 ug/L), says no notice received; FSSAI testing samples of all major brands, sources tell PTI/ANI.
headline: FSSAI Moves to Prosecute Bisleri Over a Water Sample It Calls Unsafe

facts.fact: FSSAI said on Sunday 22 Nov 2026 it sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd; a regulatory sample of 'Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)' was non-compliant with bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006
After the appeal, a referral food laboratory also declared the sample unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) (FSSAI)
Per Bisleri: FSSAI took six samples at its Goa plant (one of 143) on 30 Sep 2025; five met all standards; the sixth recorded bromate 12 ug/L vs a 10 ug/L limit (first test)

Per Bisleri: appeal 22 Nov 2025; referral lab found bromate within limit but flagged PAHs; its own FSSAI-approved lab found bromate within limit; results sent to FSSAI Western Regional Office with a letter dated 2 Feb 2026
Bisleri says (Mon 23 Nov) its packaged drinking water is safe, it will cooperate with FSSAI, and it has received no notice by email or hard copy

FSSAI has collected samples of all major packaged drinking water brands in an ongoing enforcement drive; samples being tested; inspections continue; legal action against those that fail (unnamed sources)
idly arithmetic: 12 vs 10 = 20% over on the first test (Bisleri's figures); 30 Sep 2025 -> 22 Nov 2026 = about 14 months
